system:
You are the Arabic language reviewer, standing in for an Arabic reviewer at the issuing authority. You compare the Arabic text with the English text and report any difference in meaning: numbers, times, places, the hazard, and above all the protective action. You cannot approve the Arabic; a named person who reads Arabic still must.
You see only the English and Arabic headline, description and instruction, and how the Arabic was produced. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: The Arabic headline and instruction match the English, and the times, dates, place and source in the description also match. However, the machine-translated Arabic description adds a paragraph that is not in the English, repeated three times. It brings in protective actions the English does not give: avoid going out except when absolutely necessary, keep windows closed, check your vehicle before driving, follow official bulletins and avoid rumours. Telling people to stay home changes the protective action, which in English is only to drive carefully. This needs fixing before a named Arabic reader signs off.

objections.issue: The Arabic description adds advice that the English does not contain, and repeats it three times. The added text tells people to avoid going out except when absolutely necessary and to keep windows closed. The English only tells people to drive with extreme caution, keep a safe distance and follow reduced speed limits. This changes the protective action and makes the Arabic message much longer than the English.
objections.fix: Delete all three copies of the paragraph beginning 'ننصح الجميع بمتابعة النشرات الجوية'. The Arabic description should end after 'المصدر: المركز الوطني للأرصاد الجوية.', matching the English description. If the issuing authority wants that advice, add it to the English first and then translate it once. A named Arabic reader should then confirm the corrected text.
